title: Counting Objects up to 20
seo_title: Counting Objects – Primary 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count objects from 1 to 20; match numbers to groups of objects; read and write numbers 0 to 20. (summary of the NERDC Primary 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 maths worksheets on counting objects up to 20 with pictures, one more and one less, and counting in real life. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The last number you say is how many.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Point to each object and say one number for each.
  • The last number you say tells you how many there are.
  • One more means the next number. One less means the number before.

Examples

Example

Count: ● ● ● ● ● ●

1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting an object twiceTouch each one only once.
Missing an objectCross them out as you count.
Saying the numbers too fastSay one number for each object.

How many cars are in the car park?
items.e: Count across the top row: 7 cars. Count on along the bottom row: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. There are 14 cars.

items.q: How many empty spaces are there?
items.e: Count only the empty spaces, not the cars. Top row: 3. Bottom row: 3. 3 and 3 is 6.

items.q: One more car parks. How many cars will there be?

items.q: Uche’s coat peg is number 19. The next peg is one more. What number is it?
items.e: One more than 19 is 20. 9 units and 1 more make 2 tens.

items.q: Bisi walks down 20 steps. She counts back: 20, 19, 18 … What comes after 11?
items.e: Counting back, the number after 11 is 10.
